item.title: Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78376-1

Superconducting diodes can provide nonreciprocal elements for superconducting and quantum circuits, but the role of diode efficiency in quantum-device performance remains unclear. Here, the authors demonstrate an enhanced superconducting diode effect in twisted NbSe2 and show that even a moderate degree of nonreciprocity is sufficient to stabilize anharmonic qubit circuits.
item.dc:title: Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits

item.title: Somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decision bias via the superior colliculus
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78331-0

The authors show that, when detecting the presence of tactile stimuli, mouse primary somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decisions through the midbrain superior colliculus, primarily by shifting decision bias rather than the ability to detect the stimulus.
item.dc:title: Somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decision bias via the superior colliculus

item.title: H3K27M cooperates with ASCL1 to maintain progenitor states and drive gliomagenesis
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78138-z

Histone 3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitutions (H3K27M) cause aggressive DMGs by preventing radial glial progenitor cell differentiation into oligodendrocytes. Here, the authors show that the transcription factor ASCL1 works with K27M to guide BRG1, maintaining cells in an oligodendrocyte precursor state.
item.dc:title: H3K27M cooperates with ASCL1 to maintain progenitor states and drive gliomagenesis

item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78567-w

This study develops a comprehensive pan-genome resource for Brassica napus and reveals how structural variations shape gene regulation and seed quality traits. The findings provide insights into genome diversity and crop improvement.

item.title: Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77235-3

Mentalising is essential for social interaction and is thought to rely on the medial prefrontal cortex. Here, the authors show that damage to the medial prefrontal cortex leaves mentalising intact but alters how quickly people make social decisions.

item.title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda)
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78343-w

Dinosaurs coexisted with flowering plants, but it’s unclear whether they ate them. The study presents a new small theropod dinosaur with remarkable jaw adaptations for eating fruit, providing one of the strongest evidence of dinosaur-angiosperm interaction.

item.title: Large-scale identical-location electron microscopy enables quantifying nanoparticulate electrocatalyst degradation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78329-8

Fuel cells rely on catalysts made of metal nanoparticles, but tracking how these particles wear down individually has been difficult. Here, the authors build an automated image analysis pipeline to track hundreds of platinum-cobalt nanoparticles and classify the degradation pathways they undergo.
item.dc:title: Large-scale identical-location electron microscopy enables quantifying nanoparticulate electrocatalyst degradation

item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78475-z

Corpus collosum dysgenesis is an umbrella term for all congenital malformations of the corpus callosum. Here, the authors show that corpus callosum dysgenesis is associated with intact visual perception but impaired metacognition.

item.title: Extensive genomic diversity in Desulfovibrio reveals species-specific functional traits associated with disease
item.description:
Tingting Zheng, Isabel Keidel, Hélène Omer, Akshat Joshipura, Aurélie Cenier, Ezgi Atay, Yi Han Tan, Daniela Wetzel, et al.
Nature Communications, vol. 17, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78314-1
Abstract Desulfovibrio spp. are associated with inflammatory diseases and human health, yet limited representative genomes and isolates hinder our understanding of their role in disease. Here, we assembled a comprehensive database of 2658 Desulfovibrio genomes across 90 diseases and 32 countries, including 24 human isolates. Genomic analyses showed extensive species diversity and revealed disease-associated functional traits, including flagellin and adaptation-associated genes (i.e., ureases). Flagellin-mediated Toll-like receptor 5 activation was species-specific and D. desulfuricans flagellin downregulated TGF-beta signalling in murine small intestinal organoids, suggesting impaired immune tolerance. Additionally, we investigated genomic capacity for hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) production, a main Desulfovibrio metabolite. While health- and disease-associated Desulfovibrio spp. mainly encoded dissimilatory sulfate reduction, tetrathionate metabolism-encoding bacteria were exclusively detected in inflammatory bowel diseases, including Proteus mirabilis and Morganella morganii . Overall, our study provides a comprehensive genomic Desulfovibrio resource and identifies new links associating strain variation, functional traits and H 2 S-production with inflammatory diseases.

item.title: Disability related disparities in diagnosis and survival of digestive system cancers in Northern Italy
item.description:
Flavia Pennisi, Carlotta Buzzoni, Federico Gervasi, Maria Teresa Greco, Carlo Signorelli, Antonio Giampiero Russo, Cristina Renzi
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78262-w
Abstract Individuals with disabilities may experience disparities in cancer diagnosis, but population-based evidence remains limited. We conduct a population-based cohort study using linked cancer registry and administrative healthcare data for digestive system cancers diagnosed between 2018 and 2021 in Northern Italy, examining diagnostic routes and one-year survival according to pre-existing impairments. Individuals with impairments are more likely to be diagnosed following emergency presentation compared with those without impairments (51.8% compared with 37.9%; adjusted odds ratio 1.41, 95% confidence interval 1.23–1.61), particularly those with impairments of mental and neuromusculoskeletal functions. They also have higher one-year mortality (hazard ratio 1.36, 95% confidence interval 1.26–1.46), independent of socio-demographic and clinical factors. Here, we show that disability-related disparities in emergency cancer diagnosis and survival persist across multiple impairment categories, providing population-based evidence from a European setting on differences in diagnostic pathways across heterogeneous disability groups.

item.title: Fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography using explicit neural fields
item.description:
Renzhi He, Yucheng Li, Junjie Chen, Truc M. Dinh, Charlotte R. Stevens, Aidan E. Gilchrist, Yi Xue
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78326-x
Abstract Multimodal fluorescence and phase imaging provides complementary information about biological samples. However, existing simultaneous fluorescence-phase techniques primarily operate in transmission mode and are limited to thin specimens, restricting their use in thick tissues and in vivo applications. Although multiphoton microscopy enables deep-tissue fluorescence imaging, combining it with three-dimensional refractive-index (RI) imaging remains challenging because few methods can reconstruct the RI of bulky, label-free tissues in reflection mode at subcellular resolution. Here, we introduce fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography (FDT), which reconstructs the 3D RI of label-free and fluorescence-labeled objects from diffracted fluorescence images acquired in reflection mode under two-photon excitation. FDT uses the transport of intensity equation and a self-supervised neural network based on explicit neural fields. Compared with state-of-the-art implicit neural fields, this approach improves computational speed, reconstruction accuracy, and interpretability. We demonstrate FDT in two experimental regimes: reconstructing the 3D RI of label-free tissues up to 300 μ m thick placed on a fluorescent substrate, and reconstructing the 3D RI of fluorescence-labeled, 3D-cultured cells without transmission-side access using fluorescence emitted by the cells themselves. FDT establishes a foundation for accessible reflection-mode multimodal fluorescence-phase imaging in complex biological systems.

item.title: Structural basis of ammonium transport and coordinated regulation of AMT1;1 in Arabidopsis thaliana
item.description:
Bangguo He, Ting Bai, Liyang Wang, Shuai Zhang, Wei Ying
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78457-1
Abstract Efficient ammonium uptake is essential for plant growth and nitrogen-use efficiency, yet the structural basis of ammonium transport and regulation in plant AMTs remains unclear. Here, we determined multiple cryo-electron microscopy structures of the Arabidopsis thaliana ammonium transporter AMT1;1 in apo, ammonium-bound, methylammonium-bound, low-pH and phosphomimetic states. These structures reveal a conserved ammonium conduction pathway comprising an aromatic recruitment vestibule, a Phe-gate/Twin-His-containing pore, and a polar intracellular exit region. We further identified a conserved extracellular N-terminal disulfide bond required for oligomer stability and transport activity, suggesting potential redox-dependent regulation. On the cytoplasmic side, phosphorylation modulates C-terminal interactions with intracellular loops, revealing an allosteric regulatory mechanism. Comparison with the bacterial ammonium-sensing protein Sd -Amt1 uncovers a conserved ammonium-recognition region in At AMT1;1 that contributes to transport activity but lacks the signaling module and ligand-dependent conformational switching observed in Sd -Amt1. Together, these findings provide structural insight into ammonium transport and coordinated regulation in plant AMT transporters.

item.title: CREST functions as a molecular bridge between neuron-specific enhancers and epigenetic regulators in mature motor neurons
item.description:
Kaitlin N. Montanera, Andrew J. Lee, Woobin Yun, Alyssa Ialongo Del Prete, Ssu-Yu Yeh, Inkyung Jung, Ho Sung Rhee
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78396-x
Abstract Motor neuron development requires precise transcriptional regulation mediated in part by BAF (BRG1/BRM-associated factor) chromatin remodeling complexes. The neuron-specific BAF subunit CREST is critical for neuronal function and is mutated in some cases of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), yet its underlying genomic mechanisms remain unclear. Using mouse embryonic stem cell differentiation, we show that CREST is essential for motor neuron maturation by activating mature neuronal genes and repressing progenitor genes. Mechanistically, CREST interacts with the neuronal transcription factors ONECUT1 and NGN2, and the BRM ATPase to target pre-existing accessible enhancers of neuronal genes. CREST deletion selectively prevents CBP histone acetyltransferase recruitment, reducing histone H3K27 acetylation at these enhancers and downregulating target gene expression, without disrupting BRM binding, enhancer accessibility, or long-range chromatin architecture. Overall, our findings identify CREST as a crucial epigenetic mediator bridging lineage-specific transcription factors, BAF complexes, and CBP to activate enhancers and promote proper motor neuron development.
